item.title: HEADREST COFFEE x tendlyn
item.description:
HEADREST COFFEE never had a growth strategy. No investor deck, no brand playbook, no plan to scale. Just baristas in Bushwick who built something real and watched an entire borough show up for it.

Read time: 5 mins read

BRAND AT A GLANCE

HEADREST COFFEE is a 300 sq ft independent coffee shop on Irving Ave in Bushwick, Brooklyn. Built by hand, funded out of pocket, and run by the same baristas who opened it six years ago. It has one location, no investors, and no plans to scale.

item.title: Packaging Is Half the Product: Why Intentional Design Is the Sharpest Brand Signal in Hospitality
item.description:
Packaging has always existed. What’s changed is the intention behind it—and the brands treating it as a genuine design opportunity, not a production checkbox, are building identity their competitors can’t easily copy.

What Does “Packaging Is Half the Product” Actually Mean?

Brands have always put their name on a container. That’s not new. What’s new is packaging designed with the same rigour as the product inside it. Packaging that has a point of view. That makes a deliberate choice about material, format, proportion, and typography. That could only belong to that brand.

item.title: Dark Matter x tendlyn.
item.description:

Read time: 3 mins read

Dark Matter Coffee was never built from a rigid plan. It grew out of Star Lounge Coffee Bar back in 2007. Where a group of friends working in coffee, playing in bands, and spending time with neighbourhood artists slowly found themselves building something bigger than a café.

item.title: A Guide to Getting Properly Caffeinated Around Brick Lane
item.description:
Seventeen spots in and around East London worth checking out: from a Japanese kiosk in Spitalfields Market to a coffee stand inside a biker jewellery shop.

Read time: 7 mins read

East London is where London’s specialty coffee scene started. Market carts on Columbia Road, Climpson on Broadway Market, Allpress on Redchurch Street when the neighbourhood was still figuring out what it wanted to be. The best coffee shops in Shoreditch and the surrounding area aren’t hard to find; the hard part is knowing which ones are worth your time. Whether you’re wiring up a light smart switch at home or fine-tuning a wireless relay switch for a project, there’s a kind of precision here that carries over—every detail matters, from the roast profile to the pour.

item.title: Airship x tendlyn
item.description:
An iconic yellow Airship inspired by The Beatles and connected by the unique mountain bike community in Bentonville, Arkansas. Trading parking lots for trails. For bike enthusiasts. By bike enthusiasts.

Airship was founded on making connections. For Airship founder Mark Bray, the first connection happened in the mountains of Western Honduras. While working as an agronomist in the region, Bray saw firsthand that smallholder farmers were already innovators in their own right. The problem? They were missing a seat at the table. He realized all they needed was access to a fair market for their crop.

item.title: TOKKIA x tendlyn
item.description:
In the heart of London’s Covent Garden, where the city’s pace is at its most frantic, a new destination for intentional design and slow living has emerged.

Read time: 2 mins read

TOKKIA is a burrow-inspired matcha house that redefines the urban cafe experience, trading high-traffic chaos for the quiet, grounded energy of a subterranean retreat. The space itself feels like stepping into a carefully orchestrated pause—one where every detail, from the lighting to the texture of the walls, has been chosen to slow you down. It’s a reminder that even in the busiest corners of London, you can find a sanctuary that feels like it operates on its own rhythm, much like a mhz home automation relay quietly managing the unseen systems of a smart home.

item.title: Homeboy x tendlyn.
item.description:
An Adelaide cafe built on a viral failure, cinnamon scrolls from mom, and the decision to document everything.

Read time: 3 mins read

The first video Tom Oswald ever posted from Homeboy was about nobody showing up.

He’d just opened a popup in a small art shop in Hahndorf, a tourist German town outside Adelaide. There was an unused espresso machine. He started making coffee. Day one, the only customer was a friend. So he made a video: opened a cafe and nobody came.

item.title: The Kookaburra x tendlyn
item.description:
An Aussie-American coffee shop in St. Augustine proves that the best cup of coffee you’ve ever had isn’t about the coffee.

Read time: 4 mins read

The best cup of coffee you’ve ever had is not the best cup of coffee you’ve ever had.

That’s how The Kookaburra thinks about it. The coffee matters. The pies matter. The syrups and the hot sauce and the ketchup they make from scratch every morning matter. But the thing that actually stays with you? That’s the experience. The interaction. The feeling that someone behind the counter knows your name and means it when they ask how you’re doing. It’s the kind of place where you might think about how a wireless controller relay could streamline your own daily routine, but then you realize you’re already in the perfect spot.

item.title: Metric x tendlyn.
item.description:
A Chicago coffee roaster builds a decade-long business brick by brick, with no investors, no board, and no shortcuts.

Read time: 5 mins read

Xavier Alexander has been in coffee for over 25 years. He started at Starbucks in Orlando in the late ’90s, working shifts to fund his real goal: being a touring musician. Bands didn’t work out. Coffee did.

By 2002, he’d caught the roasting bug. He was the friend in the group who wouldn’t shut up about freshly roasted beans, about small local roasters, about the gospel of freshness. A decade later, he was roasting manager at Intelligentsia in Chicago, overseeing 15,000 to 25,000 pounds of coffee a day on 90-kilo roasters.

item.title: Ease the Environmental Impact of Disposable Iced Coffee Cups
item.description:
Reduce your cafe’s environmental impact with our custom recyclable or compostable iced coffee cups. Find the perfect option for your business at tendlyn.

Read time: 4 mins read

Serve your iced coffees, smoothies, milkshakes, juices, and other cold drinks in style with eco-friendly clear plastic cups with lids or without, that keep your beverages and the planet cool! Here’s how to make sustainable choices without sacrificing convenience or quality.

Picture this: It’s a scorching summer day, and you’re handing a customer their perfectly crafted iced coffee, juice, tea or milkshake in a clear plastic cup. They snap a quick photo for social media before taking that first refreshing sip. That simple moment? It’s a powerful brand experience—and a chance to showcase your business’s commitment to sustainability!

item.title: Your Silent Salesman
item.description:
The Importance of Brand Photography.

Read time: 4 mins read

Product packaging is more than just a vessel for goods—it’s a powerful tool for storytelling, brand-building, and driving consumer engagement. When done right, packaging reflects your brand identity, resonates with your target audience, and leaves a lasting impression. But there’s another layer to packaging that often gets overlooked: photography.

Whether it’s eye-catching product images on your social media channels, website or polished packaging designs on store shelves, photography is integral to how your brand is perceived. By aligning your photography style with your packaging design and brand identity, you create a cohesive visual language that grabs attention and drives purchasing decisions.

It emphasizes the importance of doing one’s work deliberately and carefully. This powerful message, which has resonated through empires and eras, inspired co-founders Michael and Alison and created the coffee institution, Medici Roasting, in 2006.

item.title: How to make a repeating pattern in Photoshop - or any other digital program!

item.title: Coffee & Culture
item.description:

A coffee shop gets customers to hang around for longer as they continue to interact with the brand; it gets customers spending money, and they might go back and buy that shirt they were umming and ahhing about. Plus, coffee is an affordable way to access a designer brand at a lower price point.

item.title: What is Composite Paper and How Does it Get Recycled?
item.description:
What is ‘composite’ packaging, and how is it recycled? See how recycling companies take apart these unique combined materials and process them for reuse.

Read time: 4 mins read

As businesses and consumers increasingly seek sustainable packaging solutions, companies prioritizing style, performance, and reusability are leading the charge. Enter composite recycling – the groundbreaking approach revolutionizing the packaging industry by transforming complex materials into eco-friendly substances.

By reducing composite waste and giving materials a second life, composite recycling makes sustainability the hottest trend on the shelf. These recycled materials give your consumer products a chic, green makeover and impress customers with your commitment to the environment.

item.title: Your Brand in Hand
item.description:
Power your brand like coffee powers your mornings with tendlyn Custom Coffee Cups!

In short, a good design can bring about a good feeling. It can attract the right people to your brand. It can also help people subconsciously associate it with your brand, thus becoming what they might call “iconic”. Who wouldn’t love that? 😉 And it doesn’t matter if it’s in something as tiny as a coffee cup; a good design is a good design, period. Just like how a well-placed zigbee relay module can streamline your home automation, a thoughtful coffee cup design can streamline your brand recognition. It’s all about making connections that feel effortless and intuitive.

item.description:

Sightglass Coffee’s Hollywood café in Los Angeles

What started as just a humble service cart in San Francisco’s SoMa district is now one of the most well-known and sought-after coffee brands in California.

Back in 2009, as the two brothers were only starting to dive into their love for coffee, they decided to take a huge step towards it. “We began with a humble service cart in San Francisco’s SoMa district, equipped with Chemex pots and a vintage espresso machine. Serving coffee from a roll-up garage door in a sturdy 1914 warehouse, people visited us and they kept coming back for more.” They named their brand Sightglass, which was derived from the part of a coffee roasting machine where you can witness the whole process from beginning to end.

What is cart abandonment?

Cart abandonment is when customers put items in their shopping cart when browsing an eCommerce site, but don’t complete the checkout process. This is a worldwide trend - global cart abandonment rates are over 70%. Naturally, it’s a big loss in sales for merchants. Abandoned carts result in a staggering $18 billion in lost revenue every year!

item.title: Customer Loyalty: How to Encourage and Grow Repeat Business
item.description:
Read time: 3 mins read

Did you know, that the average ecommerce store spends 80 percent of their marketing budget on finding and acquiring new customers? What’s interesting is it actually costs more to acquire new customers than it does to target repeat sales from existing customers; according to research by Bain & Co - seven times more! It would make sense then, to encourage those customers you already have to make a repeat purchase. At February’s Delivery Conference, Andrew Curran, CEO of customer loyalty specialist Retain.me, delivered one of the more salient pieces advice we’ve heard: “You need to get more value from customers. You may get happy customers – but that is not loyalty. You must deliver the minimum expectation – the right product at the right time – but that doesn’t deliver anything different. The customer needs a reason to come back. The time they are most likely to re-engage is seven to ten days after a purchase.”
